current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response containing member profile information and JWT tokens for session management. This type represents the response returned after successful member authentication through registration (join), login, or token refresh operations. It includes the member's public profile information (id, email, display_name) along with JWT access and refresh tokens that enable authenticated API access to protected endpoints. The access token is a short-lived JWT (1 hour expiration) used for authorizing API requests, while the refresh token is a long-lived JWT (30 days expiration) used to obtain new access tokens without requiring re-authentication. Both tokens follow the Bearer token convention and should be included in the Authorization header of subsequent API requests.

Includes JWT tokens (access_token, refresh_token) generated server-side with 1-hour and 30-day expiration respectively. token_type is constant 'Bearer', expires_in is constant 3600 seconds. token property references IAuthorizationToken schema containing access/refresh tokens with expiration metadata. IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Lightweight article summary for list and search results displays.

This DTO provides essential article metadata optimized for browsing and search result listings. It includes the article identifier, title, section categorization, author information, and timestamps, while excluding full body content and attachment arrays to reduce payload size.

The summary includes a dynamically computed comment count reflecting the total number of comments on the article. Section and author are represented as summary objects containing only their essential identifying information.

Soft-deleted articles are automatically filtered out by the backend - this DTO only represents active articles visible to users.

Relations: section via discussion_board_section_id JOIN to discussion_board_sections, member via discussion_board_member_id JOIN to discussion_board_members. Aggregation: comments_count computed from discussion_board_comments where discussion_board_comments.article_id = discussion_board_articles.id. Soft-delete filter: only return where deleted_at IS NULL. Section and member loaded as .ISummary objects (id, name/display_name only).

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering, searching, and paginating discussion board articles.

This DTO defines the query criteria for article listing endpoints, supporting comprehensive search and filtering capabilities. Users can search articles by keyword matching across titles and body content using GIN trigram indexes, filter by specific sections or authors, apply date range filters, and paginate through results.

When multiple tag IDs are provided, the system applies AND logic, returning only articles that contain all specified tags via the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

Pagination parameters control the number of results returned per page and which page to retrieve. Sorting options allow ordering by creation date or title in ascending or descending order.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible query combinations. The server automatically excludes soft-deleted articles from results unless the deleted flag is set (admin-only).

This DTO does not directly map to a single database table but provides query parameters that filter and sort discussion_board_articles data. Implementation: search uses GIN trigram indexes on discussion_board_articles.title and discussion_board_articles.body columns. sectionId parameter filters by discussion_board_section_id foreign key column with JOIN to discussion_board_sections. memberId parameter filters by discussion_board_member_id foreign key column with JOIN to discussion_board_members. createdAtGte/createdAtLte filter discussion_board_articles.created_at timestamp column. Pagination uses page/limit with defaults page=1, limit=20, max=100, applying OFFSET and LIMIT clauses. Sorting by created_at or title with asc/desc order (default: created_at desc) via ORDER BY clause. tagIds applies AND logic via JOIN to discussion_board_article_tags junction table. deleted flag (admin-only) controls soft-delete filtering where deleted_at IS NULL by default. All parameters optional for flexible query combinations.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was originally created (ISO 8601 date-time format).
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_comments.created_at. Auto-generated on insert with current timestamp (timestamptz). Immutable after creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified (ISO 8601 date-time format).
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_comments.updated_at. Auto-updated on each modification with current timestamp (timestamptz).

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted, or null if the comment is active (ISO 8601 date-time format or null).
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_comments.deleted_at. Nullable timestamptz. NULL = active comment, set timestamp = soft-deleted comment (filtered from queries).

member.description: Author of this comment, represented as a member summary with public profile information.
member.x-autobe-specification: Relation via JOIN on discussion_board_member_id to discussion_board_members.id. Returns IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary containing author profile information (id, display_name, ban_status, created_at).

article.description: Parent article this comment belongs to, represented as an article summary with essential metadata.
article.x-autobe-specification: Relation via JOIN on discussion_board_article_id to discussion_board_articles.id. Returns IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary containing parent article information (id, title, section, author, timestamps).

IDiscussionBoardComment.description: Complete comment entity representing a single-level comment on a discussion board article. Each comment is authored by one member and belongs to exactly one article. Comments support soft deletion to preserve audit history while hiding from public views. The entity includes embedded author information (member summary) and parent article reference (article summary) to provide full context without requiring additional API calls, enabling clients to display comments with complete author and article information in a single response.
IDiscussionBoardComment.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mapping: id, discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_member_id, content, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relations: member via JOIN on discussion_board_member_id to discussion_board_members (author profile as ISummary), article via JOIN on discussion_board_article_id to discussion_board_articles (parent article as ISummary). Soft-delete semantics: deleted_at NULL = active comment, set timestamp = deleted comment (filtered from queries). Query optimization uses indexed columns discussion_board_article_id and created_at.

id.description: Unique identifier for the guest account.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_guests.id. UUID primary key generated by database.

device_fingerprint.description: Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest user across sessions.
device_fingerprint.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_guests.device_fingerprint. Unique device identifier generated from device characteristics for anonymous guest identification.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_guests.created_at. Timestamp when the guest account was created.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted, null if active.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_guests.deleted_at. Nullable timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Null indicates active account.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary.description: Lightweight guest account summary for list views and references. Contains the device fingerprint that uniquely identifies the anonymous guest across sessions. Used for displaying guest identity in session listings and other contexts where full guest details are not required.
IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_guests table. All properties map directly to database columns: id, device_fingerprint, created_at, deleted_at. Excludes updated_at (not essential for summary display) and sessions relation (HAS-MANY composition handled separately). Used for displaying guest identity in session listings and list views.

scenario.draft: Test the primary guest registration workflow where an unauthenticated visitor creates a guest account using only a device fingerprint. The system should generate a unique guest identifier, create records in both the discussion_board_guests and discussion_board_guest_sessions tables, and return JWT access and refresh tokens with expiration metadata. Validate that the response includes the generated guest ID, optional display name (null or empty when not provided), and complete token information including access token, refresh token, expired_at timestamp, and refreshable_until timestamp. This scenario validates the core anonymous browsing capability that enables guests to access sections, articles, and comments without email/password credentials.

plan.thinking: Collects IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate to discussion_board_articles. The DTO contains title, body, discussion_board_section_id, and optional tagIds in the request body. The discussion_board_member_id (author) is extracted from JWT authentication token, not from the DTO body, so it requires a reference from authorized actor. Tag associations are created in discussion_board_article_tags junction table as part of the atomic transaction.
Collects IDiscussionBoardTag.ICreate to discussion_board_tags. Create DTO for tag creation with name and description fields. All data in request body, no external FK references needed.

Collects IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate to discussion_board_comments. The DTO contains only content field; discussion_board_article_id comes from path parameter {articleId}, and discussion_board_member_id comes from authenticated member session.

IDiscussionBoardSection.ICreate is a Create DTO that maps to discussion_board_sections table. Collects section with name and description. The discussion_board_admin_id (creator) is extracted from authenticated admin session, requiring reference from authorized actor.

Collects IDiscussionBoardAdminRequest.ICreate to discussion_board_admin_requests table. The DTO contains only the reason field; discussion_board_member_id is resolved from the authenticated member's JWT token (authorized actor). This is a collectable Create DTO for administrator privilege request submission.

Collects IDiscussionBoardBanRecord.ICreate to discussion_board_ban_records table. The DTO contains discussion_board_member_id and reason in the request body, but discussion_board_admin_id is resolved from the authenticated admin actor.

Request body for super administrators to review pending administrator privilege requests. Maps to discussion_board_admin_requests table with status field (approved/rejected). Backend updates status, reviewed_at, and discussion_board_admin_id upon processing.
